text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the "single-line safe-change" flag but restrict it to mechanical fixes. This keeps auto-apply safe by limiting it to edits that don’t alter logic or intent—like typos or formatting—while avoiding risky changes to prompts or routing. The trade-off is slower iteration on meaningful improvements, but it prevents costly mistakes.

name: Gauge
text: The "single-line safe-change" flag ignores that a typo in one line often signals a systemic flaw in the prompt or routing—fixing the typo without addressing the root cause leaves the same error pattern to recur. A better alternative is to auto-apply only mechanical fixes that are provably reversible (e.g., whitespace, dead code) and route all logic-altering changes to human review; settle the argument by testing both approaches on a week of production prompts and measuring recurrence rates.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt the "provably reversible mechanical fix" rule: auto-apply only edits that can be undone by a single, obvious command. This keeps the system safe while still catching typos and formatting errors that recur across prompts. The trade-off is missing fixes that require judgment—like rewording a prompt for clarity—but those belong in human review to avoid unintended shifts in behavior.

name: Gauge
text: The "provably reversible mechanical fix" rule still misses the real risk: even reversible edits can mask deeper flaws. A typo in a prompt might seem fixable by a simple revert, but if the underlying prompt structure is flawed, the same error will keep appearing—just in a different form. Settle this by tracking recurrence rates of the same error across prompts; if the same typo or formatting issue keeps coming back after fixes, the rule isn’t solving the problem—it’s just hiding it.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply only edits that are *both* provably reversible *and* context-free mechanical—like fixing typos or formatting—while routing all other changes to manual review.

Result must deliver: a clear rule set for safe auto-apply edits, with a flagging system that catches deeper flaws in prompts or routing. Owner: Sprocket.
